SF-614.summary: Derive and maintain Is_Active__c on Member Legal Entity Relationship records
SF-614.description:
Member Legal Entity Relationship records do not have a user-managed status field. The relationship’s active/inactive state must be derived from Start and End dates and stored on the record to provide a clear, consistent indicator for downstream integrations and reporting. 

As a Integration User 
I want the active/inactive state of a Member Legal Entity Relationship to be explicitly derived and stored
So that downstream systems can reliably determine the lifecycle state without re-deriving business logic. 

Background:
Given the Member Legal Entity Relationship object exists in Salesforce 
And the relationship uses Start and End Dates to represent its lifecycle
And downstream systems require an explicit Active/Inactive indicator for the relationships. 

Scenario: Is_Active__c field exists on Member Legal Entity Relationship
Given the Member Legal Entity Relationship object exists
Then a new field named "Is_Active__c" should be created
And it must be populated based on Start and End Dates
And it must be hidden from the UI page layout for all users
And it must be available to integration users and system administrators

Scenario: Is_Active__c is set to Active when Start Date is reached and the End Date is blank
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
And Start Date is on or before today
And End Date is blank
When the record is created or updated
Then Is_Active__c is set to true

Scenario: Is_Active__c is set to Active when the Start Date is reached and the End Date is in the future
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
And Start Date is on or before today
And End Date is on or after today
When the record is created or updated
Then Is_Active__c is set to true

Scenario: Is_Active__c is set to Inactive when Start Date is in the future
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
And Start Date is after today
When the record is created or updated
Then Is_Active__c is set to false

Scenario: Is_Active__c is set to Inactive when End Date is in the past
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
And End Date is before today
When the record is created or updated
Then Is_Active__c is set to false

Scenario: Is_Active__c is recalculated when Start Date or End Date changes
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
When Start Date or End Date is updated
Then Is_Active__c is recalculated based on the updated dates

Scenario: Is_Active__c is set to Active when End Date is changed from past to future
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
And Start Date is on or before today
And End Date is before today
And Is_Active__c is false
When the End Date is updated to a date on or after today
Then Is_Active__c is recalculated
And Is_Active__c is set to true

Scenario: Is_Active__c is recalculated when the date changes and causes a status transition
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
And Is_Active__c is true
And End Date is tomorrow
When the current date becomes the day after tomorrow
Then Is_Active__c is set to false

Scenario: Is_Active__c transitions occur only when the derived status changes
Given a Member Legal Entity Relationship record exists
When the relationship dates do not cause a change in derived status
Then Is_Active__c remains unchanged

Permissions and Visibility
Is_Active__c is a system-derived field and must be hidden from user interfaces
